gaps.sentence: We will lose the deposit if we ___ the booking now.
gaps.explanation: The result clause carries 'will'; the if-clause stays in the present simple: cancel.

gaps.sentence: We will refund the item provided that you ___ the receipt.
gaps.hint: provided that plus a present requirement
gaps.explanation: 'Provided that' states a requirement using the present simple: have.

gaps.sentence: If the taxi ___ in five minutes, we are going to miss our flight.
gaps.hint: real future risk in the if-clause
gaps.explanation: Real future conditions take the present simple in the if-clause: does not arrive.

gaps.sentence: If you order before midnight, delivery ___ nothing.
gaps.hint: result clause of a first conditional
gaps.explanation: The result of a real future condition takes 'will': will cost.

gaps.sentence: If he ___ so stubborn, we would have reached an agreement by now.
gaps.hint: present cause with a result up to now
gaps.explanation: An unreal present cause can produce a result reaching into the past; formally 'were' is used: were not.

gaps.sentence: If only I ___ more free time these days.
gaps.hint: if only plus past, present wish
gaps.explanation: 'If only' works like 'wish' and takes the past simple for present regrets: had.

gaps.sentence: If the pilot ___ the storm, we would have landed on time.
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition takes the past perfect: had avoided.

gaps.sentence: If you had set an alarm, you ___.
gaps.explanation: The present result of a past unreal condition takes 'would not be': would not still be asleep.
